instruction: When the requirement review and the correctness review disagree, treat it as a finding that the acceptance criterion named the wrong observable, and fix the AC as well as the code.
outcome: An AC's letter can be met while the mechanism is unsound.

instruction: Research before answering or coding: name the existing code that does the nearest thing and extend it. Gather evidence first, cite file:line, and never assert from memory.
outcome: Directive #54. Prevents duplicate code and ungrounded claims.
owner_words: no duplicate code; cite file:line

instruction: Have the product owner write a binding spec that holds the product to the approved design or prototype EXACTLY.
outcome: Directive #55.

instruction: Give the judge an explicit product objective to hold every artifact against (here: the most advanced and most user-friendly product of its kind).
outcome: Directive #56.

instruction: Have the judge score each feature against a per-feature evaluation file: the approved design's exact values generated by script, rendered screens scored against reference shots with calibrated thresholds, and the judge's own criteria.
outcome: Directive #58. REQ-305 uses docs/product/cloud-onboarding/agent-setup/EVALUATION.md.

instruction: Have every agent read the evaluation file, the shared context file and the judge's rulings first, so the judge's metrics are the team's metrics.
outcome: Directive #59.

instruction: Plan before executing: gather every data point bearing on the instruction (code, tests, git history, prior results, live config/device state) and form an explicit plan. Never blind-fire, and never re-derive settled facts.
outcome: Standing principle.

instruction: Query the code graph before proposing, reviewing or scoping any change, so you work from the real call graph and blast radius.
outcome: Owner directive 2026-09-14.
owner_words: use of codegraph is a must and very important

instruction: Treat the code graph as a navigation aid, never an oracle: cite only file:line from a direct read or grep, treat absence from the graph as no evidence, and say which parts of a claim came from the graph and which you verified directly.
outcome: Fuzzy start-node matching: a deleteOrder query also returned getResponsiveBorderRadius and a blueprint-doc node (L-1).

instruction: Any document claiming a COMPLETE enumeration ('every writer of', 'all call sites') must cite the query or grep that produced it, or the commit is refused.
outcome: The C10 class (a fix applied at one call site while siblings bypass it) has cost the repo more than any other. 7 of 132 existing fix docs would have tripped the check when it landed; they are grandfathered by a ratchet baseline.

instruction: Ask the graph for the SHAPE of a defect to enumerate the whole class, then let evidence pick which members to fix. Never edit every member blind.
outcome: One query returned 241 unflexed Rows containing Text across 52 files in seconds. Editing all 241 blind would be guessing; the app's crash reporter names the real overflows.

instruction: Keep the code graph fresh automatically from a post-commit hook that is incremental, detached (never delays a commit), code-only (no API key, no tokens) and single-flight, defers above a load ceiling or while test runners are live, and logs deferrals.
outcome: Without single-flight, twenty worktrees would start twenty builds. A graph build competing with suites would repeat the load-137 incident.

instruction: Check code-graph freshness before trusting it (rc 0 fresh, 1 stale, 2 absent) and refresh manually when stale.
outcome: Stale graphs mislead navigation.

instruction: Do not treat a path that appears only in an ignore or guard pattern as a missing artifact. An empty guard is the correct state.
outcome: On 2026-09-14 the absence of .code-review-graph/ was briefly mistaken for a gap; it is only a pre-commit block pattern.

instruction: Research deeply before answering. Name the existing code that does the nearest thing and extend it. Gather evidence first, cite file:line, and never assert from memory.
outcome: Owner directive #54. No separate measurement.

instruction: Start every feature, fix or requirement from ONE user-visible outcome sentence and run it through the outcome-first workflow (req, outcome, path, binding, proofTest). A non-outcome task workflow refuses to run without a proven outcome.
outcome: Owner directive #65, the strict rule. No measurement recorded.
owner_words: outcome driven development only- strict rule

instruction: Trace the outcome's path on the current tree and fix only the blockers on that path, each proven RED first.
outcome: No measurement recorded.

instruction: Everything outside the current outcome is the NEXT outcome and is never mixed into this one. Run passes back to back until every task is complete.
outcome: No measurement recorded.

instruction: Score each feature against a per-feature evaluation file: exact design values, rendered screens against reference shots with calibrated bars, and the judge's own written criteria.
outcome: No measurement recorded.

instruction: In the first spec or design round, run three parallel lens judges (correctness, owner/user, testability) and merge their findings into one revision.
outcome: No measurement recorded.

instruction: A fix doc maps each failure class the diff touches to a test id. A checker fails when a class applies and no row exists.
outcome: No measurement recorded.

instruction: Query the code graph before proposing, reviewing or scoping a change. Answer 'what calls X / who writes Y' with a callers query, then do a bounded read.
outcome: ~22.2M tokens to open a large file vs 26,600 for the callers query.

instruction: Treat the graph as a navigation aid, never an oracle. Cite only file:line you opened with Read or Grep, and say which parts of a claim came from the graph and which you verified directly.
outcome: Lesson L-1: graph matching is fuzzy, and absence from the graph is not absence from the code.

instruction: A design or fix doc that claims a complete enumeration ('every writer of', 'all call sites') must cite the query or grep that produced it.
outcome: The C10 class (a fix at one call site while siblings bypass it) cost the repo more than any other failure class. 7 of 132 existing fix docs would have tripped the policy.
owner_words: use of codegraph is a must and very important

instruction: Enumerate the CLASS with one shape query, then let evidence pick which members to fix. Never edit every member blind.
outcome: One query returned 241 unflexed Row-with-Text sites across 52 files in seconds.

instruction: Check the code graph's freshness before trusting it, and refresh it incrementally (post-commit hook, code-only, no API key).
outcome: The graph was 35 days and 1,737 commits old: 840 files had changed, deleted files were still named and 634 existing files had no node. Its blast-radius answers were confident and wrong.

instruction: An acceptance criterion no run can satisfy is a requirements defect: fix it at the AC, never waive it. Grade on the corrected observable and state both forms.
outcome: Two ACs shipped that no run could meet (L-7). Fifteen surfaced in one rig window, every one the requirements owner's.

instruction: When the two reviews disagree (letter met, mechanism unsound), the AC named the wrong observable. Record which, then fix the AC as well as the code.
outcome: No measurement recorded.

instruction: Fix every issue as spec, then plan, then tasks, then TDD. Spec: defect plus correct behaviour in a per-issue doc. Plan: files, approach and a backward-compatibility note. Tasks: a checklist in the doc, mirrored in the session task list. TDD: failing test first, minimal fix, green, no analyzer or test regressions.
outcome: No measurement recorded.
enforcement: pre-commit device-verification box check on docs/fixes/*.md

instruction: Ask what the data says before changing code. Measure the production-shaped data before designing against it.
outcome: 6,144 of 6,180 'pending' orders had no items and no value; only ~34 open orders were real. Querying first would have reframed the fix in minutes.

instruction: Before inventing a symbol, import or schema, ground it with a script (exists, symbol, import, schema, similar). Lint rule templates for swallowed-error patterns.
outcome: No measurement recorded.

instruction: Before treating a missing artifact as a gap, check whether the repo only references it as a defensive ignore/guard pattern; an empty guard is the correct state, so do not go looking for it.
outcome: On 2026-09-14 the absence of .code-review-graph/ was briefly mistaken for a gap; nothing generates or reads it, it exists only as a block-staging pattern.

instruction: Never tell agents to rely on a code index/graph without a mechanical freshness check and an automatic refresh; measure staleness before trusting any blast-radius answer from it.
outcome: On 2026-09-14 the graph agents had been told to consult since August was 35 days and 1,737 commits old: 840 code files had changed under it, it still named deleted files, and 634 existing files had no node, including the whole lib/invariants/ layer. Every blast-radius answer would have been confident and wrong, and nothing caught it because nothing looked.
enforcement: scripts/verify/graph_freshness.sh (rc 0 fresh, 1 stale, 2 absent) + .githooks/post-commit incremental refresh

instruction: Treat an acceptance criterion the delivered work cannot satisfy as a defect in the AC: fix it at the AC, never waive it.
outcome: The repo shipped two ACs that no run could ever meet (lesson L-7).

instruction: When the fault is the requirement's (dead driver, wrong observable, unmeetable bar), attribute it to the requirement owner and fix the AC. Change no implementing agent's persona: agents are not penalised for following a bad card.
outcome: Standing rule; no measurement given.

instruction: For every issue, write a fix spec first: the defect and the correct behaviour, in a per-issue doc.
outcome: Mandatory per-issue loop spec -> plan -> task -> TDD.
enforcement: pre-commit checks the fix doc's verification box

instruction: Every change must leave already-deployed clients working. A client that can no longer sync cannot receive the fix, so a break is a lost device, not a later bug.
outcome: Mixed fleets of older builds sync against the same data.

instruction: Make no remote document-shape changes and no field renames; existing key-casing mappings are load-bearing.
outcome: Backward-compatibility hard constraint.

instruction: Make schema changes additive migrations only; new fields are optional with safe defaults.
outcome: Backward-compatibility hard constraint.

instruction: Absorbed items keep their ids as acceptance rows on the absorbing branch, so nothing is descoped. An item that is an instance of an in-flight invariant is never dispatched separately.
outcome: Worked examples: REQ-161 (four cards, one seam), REQ-162 (three cards, one capability).

instruction: Never fragment one defect that is reachable through several surfaces into several items with separate ladders.
outcome: REQ-149, 155, 157 and 158 were one invariant resolving through one seam, yet four ladders were queued for them; this restated directive #41, which had been written down and not followed.
enforcement: dispatch_check.sh names open cards sharing source files

instruction: Run a script over the whole set to see the distribution, because the systemic answer lives in the distribution that per-item agents cannot see.
outcome: The script showed that 44 of 53 branches shared one blocker; the backlog was one piece of work, not 53.

instruction: Waste no tokens, and make every piece of work traceable to the requirement, plan and task it serves.
outcome: Owner directive #64; became judge checks 7-10 and the context budget.
owner_words: not a single token should be wasted and all the work being done must be aligned with requirement, plan, task

instruction: Every requirement names a headline test whose assertion IS the acceptance criterion as the user experiences it (a 'Headline test:' line in the spec). Seam and unit tests support it but never certify alone.
outcome: Stops certifying on internal-seam tests that pass while the user-visible outcome fails. Promoted to a policy check.
enforcement: POLICY 9b in scripts/policy_check.sh (line required; named file must exist)

instruction: Give agents domain expertise: keep a domain-rules file and inject it into every agent at spawn.
outcome: 18 domain rules injected at spawn.

instruction: When a dead mechanism served a real need, replace it with a properly designed policy; deleting it is not enough.
outcome: The dead archiver was replaced by a real retention policy (REQ-106).
owner_words: design a real retention policy in its place

instruction: At commit, refuse a new card that names a source file an open card already names, unless it says why it is separate. Refuse to dispatch an absorbed card.
outcome: Prevents one defect being split into duplicate cards.

instruction: Run a script over the whole set to see the distribution; the systemic answer lives there, and per-item agents cannot see it.
outcome: All 53 branches had zero conflicts, and 44 were blocked by one policy that landed after they were written. The backlog was one piece of work, not 53.

instruction: State the product objective as a ranked list and order the backlog by it. Here: seamless end-to-end journey, staff productivity, best UI, best features, robustness, perfect self-guided setup.
outcome: Ruling D6 re-ranked the backlog against the objective.
owner_words: We need to be cognizant about requirement, we need the POS app which is seamless and working end to end with better productivity and it should be best in the world with best UI, best features, best robust; it has a self-guided flow to set up cloud and set up printers.
enforcement: judge charter objective line; DECISIONS.md D6

instruction: Do not dispatch a card that moves none of the objective's elements. Every new card names which element it moves.
outcome: Keeps the backlog aligned to the objective.
enforcement: every new card names which of (1)-(6) it moves

instruction: Research deeply before answering: gather the evidence and cite it.
outcome: No measurement recorded.

instruction: Score each feature against an evaluation file: the approved design's exact values generated by script, screenshots scored against reference shots with calibrated bars, plus the judge's own criteria.
outcome: First instance: the agent-setup EVALUATION.md for REQ-305.
owner_words: judge should have an evaluation criteria that exactly matches preview, and he should come up other evaluation criterias to build the most advanced pos system ever built and most user friendly.

instruction: Make the first spec and design round three parallel lens judges (correctness, owner, testability), merged into one revision.
outcome: Spec and design had taken 13 serial rounds (190 minutes) on REQ-306.
owner_words: i will go by your proposal make the rule to save tokens

instruction: Start every feature, fix or requirement from ONE owner-visible outcome sentence and run it through the outcome-first workflow.
outcome: D163/D164 had moved three requirements off the full swarm, which certified polish while the owner's outcome went unproven.
owner_words: outcome driven development only- strict rule
enforcement: CLAUDE.md JUDGED SWARM item 2; .claude/workflows/outcome-first.js; judge.md 'Outcome-driven only'; directives_check.sh

instruction: Trace the outcome's path on the current tree, and fix only the gaps that block it, each RED first.
outcome: Keeps work inside the outcome's boundary.
owner_words: ensure you stick to outcome driven development which we agreed before

instruction: Never mix work that is off the current outcome's path into it. It becomes the next outcome, with its own sentence, path and end-to-end proof test.
outcome: A 'complete all tasks' push spent three hours on backlog tasks (85 to 191 of 340) while the outcome stayed unreached.
owner_words: look like outcome driven development phylosophy is failing

instruction: Make the non-outcome task runner refuse to start without evidence that the outcome is proven (the decision id or evidence path of the real-system proof).
outcome: The backlog is delivered through outcome-first, not the plain runner.

instruction: Never dispatch, run or report a task without ONE owner-visible outcome sentence and the evidence that proves it. A task that maps to no outcome is not started, and a judge cuts it.
outcome: Reaffirmed after drift.
owner_words: Please don't leave my outcome driven approach ever, all tasks you are doing must have an outcome

instruction: Pin ambiguous requirement terms with the owner's answers immediately, and record the pinned definitions in the requirement.
outcome: 'Seat' was pinned the same minute to mean one account, along with the trial length and the payment channel.

instruction: Have the server stamp time-limited entitlements (trials), never the device clock. A reinstall or a second device never restarts them.
outcome: Closes clock-tampering and reinstall abuse.

instruction: Write entitlements only on the server, after verifying the purchase with the store; no client path can grant one. Grants to the owner's own accounts go through an audited admin act.
outcome: The money rule applied to licensing.

instruction: Use only lawful, standard, enforceable legal clauses. Version-stamp and record each acceptance, and have a lawyer review before shipping.
outcome: A blanket 'nobody can sue' clause is unenforceable in most places, so the terms take the enforceable form.
owner_words: use always legal clauses ... Dont do anything illegal

instruction: Give the requirements-owner role a single job: decide WHAT is built and in what order, defined as outcomes. It never writes code and never designs systems.
outcome: Role separation is the base of the pipeline: the PO owns outcomes and priority, the BSA owns system constraints, the Architect owns HOW (product-owner.md:98). No measurement given.
enforcement: agent tools list (product-owner.md:4: WebSearch, WebFetch, Read, Write, Edit, Glob, Grep; no Bash)

instruction: Research before writing requirements, never from memory. Search the live web for category leaders, what users praise and complain about, and what is table stakes versus a differentiator. Cite every finding.
outcome: This is the market-research step that seeds the backlog. No recorded measurement of its effect.

instruction: For every table-stakes capability, name what the best version does differently. Make some backlog items differentiators grounded in a gap you actually found in the research.
outcome: Keeps the backlog from being a feature-parity copy of competitors. Unmeasured.

instruction: Write the backlog to one requirements file in this order: vision, market evidence, differentiators, then numbered requirements. Each requirement has a user story, acceptance criteria, a MoSCoW priority and its evidence.
outcome: Produced docs/product/<slug>/REQUIREMENTS.md as the backlog of record. Unmeasured.

instruction: Order the backlog by value: walking skeleton first, then differentiators, then polish.
outcome: Sets the default sequencing of the initial backlog. Unmeasured.

instruction: When asked for the next requirement, return exactly ONE: the highest-priority undelivered one, with its full user story and ACs. First read the activity log and product folder, and adjust the backlog to what has actually shipped.
outcome: Requirements are released one at a time against the real state, not a stale plan. Unmeasured.

instruction: Declare the product COMPLETE, with a closing summary, only when every must-have and should-have has shipped AND been verified.
outcome: Gives the pipeline a defined, evidence-based end state. Unmeasured.

instruction: ACs are the contract: machine-judgeable or not released. Before release, re-read each AC for a comparative with no number ('quickly', 'smallest', 'recent'). Supply the value, its unit and a one-line reason, or file a numbered PO default with your proposed answer.
outcome: Earned in the REQ-030 round: the AC 'smallest supported height' cost a BSA round-trip before it became 600 dp.

instruction: An AC states an observable outcome and a measured envelope, never an internal mechanism symbol whose source you have not opened. Before naming a function in a measurement, read the calling line and confirm its shape (awaited, unawaited or concurrent). Once you write 'mechanism is the Architect's call', the AC holds no internal symbol.
outcome: REQ-030 AC1 bound a timing to manualSync, which main.dart runs unawaited, so it measured the wrong chain. Test reports name mechanisms by inference, and ACs make them binding.

instruction: Never write a removal or deletion set from recall. Build it from a read of the whole enclosing scope plus a repo-wide grep of each member across every source and test root. Write 'removal set closed by scan <date>', or delegate enumeration to the analyst as a named default. An upstream residual note says where to scan; it is not the set.
outcome: REQ-030 AC2 named 4 of 8 orphans in an 8-line file.

instruction: Every card carries an enumerated Acceptance list. Every AC names an OBSERVABLE that a run can assert, never a primitive, a mechanism, a proof shape or a count.
outcome: Makes each requirement outcome-checkable by a test or run. Also checked as dispatch criterion 4 (product-owner.md:146).
enforcement: scripts/pipeline/po_dispatch_check.sh (refuses a card with no enumerated acceptance list)

instruction: Split a multi-component requirement into sub-cards before its first seam merges.
outcome: Keeps each deliverable and its acceptance small and independently provable. Unmeasured.

instruction: When a verifier proves an AC unmeetable, fix the AC in the same pass and date the amendment on the card. An AC no run can satisfy is a requirements-owner defect: fix it at the AC, grade on the corrected observable, and state both forms.
outcome: Fifteen unsatisfiable ACs surfaced in one rig window, all the PO's and none a runner's (CLAUDE.md earned method 8 and its history).
enforcement: scripts/pipeline/card_check.sh (BINDING id B-4 must stay in the card)

instruction: One line above the ACs, name the victim (who is affected when it fires), today's workaround and its cost. Argue priority from that line and the service impact, never from reachability ('live in every shipped build' is not a priority argument). Say when the requirement enters net-new, unmodelled domain.
outcome: REQ-042 and REQ-043 both landed MUST on near-identical 'live in every shipped build' grounds, so sequencing had to be ruled on file locality instead of merit.

instruction: Every headline AC names its DRIVER, proven by a caller grep run this pass. For a UI gesture, name both widgets and the single mounted subtree that contains them.
outcome: Earned by three un-failable ACs in two days (REQ-030 AC1(e), REQ-042 AC1, REQ-059 AC1), all the PO's.

instruction: Every headline AC names its RED BUILD. Instrumentation the requirement adds ships as a separate, earlier commit, so the failing state is observable before the fix.
outcome: Same incident set as the DRIVER rule: three un-failable ACs.

instruction: Every headline AC names its COMPETING WRITERS (other paths to the same observable within one user action) and how the AC tells them apart. Otherwise write 'no competing writer, scan <date>'.
outcome: Stops an AC passing because a different code path produced the observable. Same incident set (history:585-588).

instruction: Make an ABSENCE claim in an AC only after grepping for and quoting the inverse path. Otherwise write the bounded form or the true inertness. A tester disproving the PREMISE has invalidated the leg, not passed it.
outcome: Stops false 'never happens' premises from becoming passing tests. Unmeasured.

instruction: Check a removal against every AC that depends on the code being removed. Say literally whether the set is wrappers or methods, and scope 'read-only' to its noun, never to a whole screen.
outcome: Stops a deletion silently breaking another AC's dependency. Unmeasured.

instruction: When intaking a defect, follow the chain to the actual WRITE. The enclosing method's guard is not the call site's guard, and a queued or replayed path lands elsewhere. Rate nothing 'theoretical' or 'guarded' without walking it to the wire.
outcome: REQ-043: the PO rated one call site 'guarded' by an untraced precondition (it queues, and the replay publishes verbatim) and another 'theoretical' when it was live from three screens.

instruction: Nothing floats unowned. Every defect, residual, stale file, test finding, judge note or incident becomes a requirement, a fold or a recorded won't-fix before the in-flight work merges. While the MUST wave clears, intake is triage-only into a findings file; promote only a MUST, an in-flight blocker or an owner ask, and report the findings count.
outcome: Residuals become tracked work, while triage-only intake stops the backlog growing during a must-wave. The charter cites POLICY 9f as the rejection point.
enforcement: POLICY 9f per the charter (the label was not found by grep in scripts/policy_check.sh)

instruction: Remove dead code only after impact analysis; DELETE is not the default verdict. For each candidate, paste a grep across all source, test and script roots run that pass, then rule WIRE (correct, should be reached), DELETE (zero callers, nothing should reach it; state the capability lost) or KEEP. A method is not dead until every call site is enumerated. When a ratchet floor drops, update its baseline in the same commit.
outcome: Protects correct-but-unwired code (e.g. a filter that should be wired, not deleted). Unmeasured.

instruction: The requirements owner does not write the spec; it releases the requirement so the analyst runs the specify skill. If the requirement is underspecified, run the clarify skill. Never skip a spec-driven stage in dispatch (analyst: specify, architect: plan, developer: tasks then implement, tester: analyze), and tell each agent which skill to open. Coding before those skills ran is the requirements owner's process defect.
outcome: Enforces the spec -> plan -> tasks -> implement chain at dispatch time. Unmeasured.

instruction: Name a MECHANISM on a card only from a command run this pass, followed to the deciding line and pasted. A log line is a HYPOTHESIS. Otherwise write 'mechanism unverified, analyst to establish'.
outcome: The PO carded a PIN check as comparing against the stored user PIN after stopping one hop early. The gate actually compared against a default, so three ACs named observables no build could produce. It was a recurrence, escalated to the owner.

instruction: Verify a consequence chain from its FIRST link. Grep and paste the call site that makes A -> B true before writing A -> B -> C.
outcome: Earned in CO-021 / D-016-PROBE.

instruction: Run every acceptance bar against the UNFIXED tree. If it already passes there, restate it as the POSITIVE outcome a broken run cannot fake (e.g. completed == true, N of N).
outcome: Earned in CO-021 D-021-AC: a bar that passes on broken code proves nothing.

instruction: An AC that names the command producing its observable cites the line inside the branch that command actually takes: grep the flag in the script and read the enclosing if/else.
outcome: Earned in REQ-107 J-1.

instruction: Before minting a new requirement id, grep unmerged branches and reports for a reservation of that id. A hit reserves it.
outcome: Ids pointed at by a report were minted for unrelated cards, so a merged main would have recorded eight unpinned refusals and an unrun script as owned by cards that do not own them.

instruction: Before ranking a requirement, grep its victim screen's constructor chain back to the app entry point or route table. If the chain dies in the known-unreachable set, the severity is LATENT and it ranks as tooling debt.
outcome: REQ-061 was ranked #2 on a victim line behind a dead screen chain, and six of eight device legs were unmeetable on any build (business-system-analyst.md:217-219).

instruction: Never mint a requirement id above the board's max. Number residuals as <OWNING-REQ>-R-n.
outcome: Earned in REQ-030 to REQ-063.

instruction: Citations are produced, not inherited. Every file:line, count and enumeration comes from a command run THIS pass, cited as 'Symbol (file:NN, re-read <date>)'. For a count carrying a safety argument, paste the command and its output and subtract definition and comment hits. If you cannot run it, cite the symbol alone with 'line not re-grounded'.
outcome: Shared working agreement 11. It superseded the BSA's 'never assert from memory' clause (business-system-analyst.md:202-203). An unearned date stamp is a false verification claim.

instruction: End every step with one definitive outcome: DONE with its output path and the passing check, INCOMPLETE with the exact remainder, or BLOCKED with the reason. Prose is not an outcome. Over budget with no output is INCOMPLETE, and that counts as success.
outcome: Makes every step's result checkable.

instruction: The system analyst never writes production code.
outcome: Role boundary.

instruction: Verify each requirement against the real system, starting from the code graph. Query it first for the mechanism, then confirm every node it names by reading the file. The graph LOCATES; only file:line from read or grep may be CITED. Its matching is fuzzy, and absence from the graph is never evidence of absence.
outcome: The graph surfaces the sibling writer a grep you did not think to run would miss (the C10 class: a fix applied at one call site while siblings bypass it).

instruction: Run the code-graph freshness check first. If it reports STALE, say so in the analysis and fall back to grep.
outcome: The graph was found 35 days and 1,737 commits behind, blind to 634 existing files, while the charter already told agents to consult it.

instruction: Attribute a duration (delay, hang, silent window) to the awaited call chain, never to a symbol name. Classify each call as awaited, unawaited or fire-and-forget, follow only the awaited chain to the leaf holding the time, and report explicitly when that corrects the claim you were handed.
outcome: REQ-030 section 1.3 overturned a test report that blamed manualSync. Concurrent work dominated the logs while adding nothing to the awaited duration.

instruction: Surface every collision between the requirement and the hard constraints (backward compatibility, sync model, money protections, behaviour users depend on). Name each one with evidence and propose the reconciliation.
outcome: Conflicts are caught before design. Unmeasured.

instruction: Rewrite the requirement as system-level specifications: affected components with citations, and data-model deltas that are additive only and carry defaults.
outcome: Grounded spec handed to the architect.

instruction: For any multi-client or distributed system, state what EACH of two clients must observe for every requirement (a two-device table).
outcome: REQUIRED for every requirement in this repo.

instruction: Answer the service questions with citations: (a) which operating phase exercises this and what differs in each; (b) when two clients hold the same record, which wins and what the loser's screen shows; (c) what users can still DO while the failure runs, and what the FIX removes. 'The user retries' is a workaround: name it and cost it.
outcome: REQ-043's double-tender was question (b) verbatim, and the PO had to produce it after the fact. REQ-037's analysis stopped at 'invisible on that till' and never reached the re-key -> kitchen-fires-twice harm.

instruction: List the edge cases and failure modes the ACs missed, the open questions for the requirements owner (ambiguities you refuse to guess) and the inputs the architect needs.
outcome: Ambiguity goes back upstream instead of being guessed. Unmeasured.

instruction: Before citing any guard (flag, timer, lock, in-flight set) as a safety property, put a four-column ledger in the analysis: SET sites, CLEAR sites, the condition each reset depends on, and the reachable state where NO reset runs. Check both teardown paths (dispose and logout -> dwell -> re-login). A reset that lives only on a success path LATCHES. A safety fact without its ledger is demoted to an open architect input.
outcome: Judge finding A2: a background-sync flag was cited as a guard from its set line alone, and both resets were unreachable on an all-null round. The latch was reachable in a shipped build (agent-product-owner.md history:606-610).

instruction: End the analysis with a gate verdict: READY FOR ARCHITECTURE, or BLOCKED with the specific questions.
outcome: Gives the stage an explicit pass/fail outcome.

instruction: Run the check you name, in the same pass, and report its output, grounding every claim at file:line. Ground every driver you hand a test plan by its own caller grep: an entry point with zero callers sends the test somewhere production never goes.
outcome: The systemic-gap command was named but not run; the PO ran it and found a fourth merge publisher that had survived four reviews. manualSync was offered as a live driver with zero callers.

instruction: The analyst opens and follows the specify skill before writing the spec, and never improvises a second specify process. A prose analysis with no skill pass is not a completed stage.
outcome: Owner directive that spec-driven stages run at each step.
owner_words: speckit at each stage

instruction: An ABSENCE claim ('zero X between A and B') is TRANSITIVE. Enumerate every callee invoked in the range and grep each for the signal (one level mandatory, two for private helpers), pasting the greps for the range and the callees. Run the headline RED test before the verdict.
outcome: REQ-023 claimed an update method never notifies, but a callee it invokes did notify. The PO promoted it to MUST on that word, the architect's headline RED was already GREEN on main, and REQ-023b was parked at design.

instruction: Never reuse an identifier namespace a checker parses. Label test-ladder rungs 'leg 0', 'leg 1', never with the lesson prefix 'L-<n>'.
outcome: The REQ-098 spec was refused by the policy checker for citing a non-existent lesson L-0 that was really its own rung label.
enforcement: scripts/policy_check.sh (treats every L-<digits> as a lesson citation); card_check.sh (BSA B-3)

instruction: Reachability is TRANSITIVE: prove the chain, never one hop. Before naming a screen or entry point as a driver or test route, grep for a constructor call outside its own file, in a file not itself unreachable, and repeat to the app entry or route table. A dead chain is a card correction: mark the legs through it NOT PRODUCIBLE and name the wiring requirement.
outcome: REQ-061's analysis called a dead screen a 'live production constructor', and the architect, developer and tester inherited 'live' verbatim. Six of eight device legs were unmeetable on any build.
enforcement: scripts/gates/reachability_gate.sh (one-hop by design, so the recursion is manual)

instruction: Hand over ONE artifact: put system grounding, conflicts and requirements-owner questions inside the spec, as its Assumptions plus an appended '## System grounding' section.
outcome: One artifact, not two, for the next stage.

instruction: Write Success Criteria that are measurable and technology-agnostic. An AC that reads PASS on a build where the check never ran is a defect: fix it before handover.
outcome: Keeps outcomes falsifiable. Unmeasured.

instruction: Keep a project constitution that restates the hard constraints so a constitution check can grade them mechanically. Where it disagrees with the project instructions file, the instructions file wins: the constitution is the defect, and say so.
outcome: Makes the source of truth unambiguous.

instruction: Never run scaffolding scripts that write a repo-global mutable 'active feature' pointer when several agents work concurrently. Write the per-requirement spec directory directly.
outcome: The shared pointer is a cross-agent clobber that silently redirects another agent's output. An architect spotted it and declined to run the script, so this is a near-miss, not an incident.

instruction: Re-derive any command or protocol table inherited from a requirement against the vendor reference before passing it downstream. Two tells stop the work: parameters that are digits of other parameters in the same list, and a field described as a serial where the cited table names no serial.
outcome: An unchallenged printer-command table became a false identity key in the design (REQ-233 P0, judge finding B-2).

instruction: Query the code graph before you list call sites, scope a blast radius or claim a change is confined. The graph only locates candidates; the file:line you cite must come from reading the file with Read or Grep.
outcome: Guards against failure class C10: the sibling site nobody listed. The rule was earned when a sibling site was missed, but this file gives no measurement of how much it paid.
enforcement: none (charter text); graph freshness via scripts/verify/graph_freshness.sh

instruction: Something missing from the code graph may still exist in the code. Check graph freshness first. If the graph is stale or absent, say so in your report, fall back to a targeted grep, and never quote the stale graph.
outcome: Stops agents treating fuzzy graph matching as proof. When the graph misses something, the fallback is a targeted search, never opening everything.

instruction: Produce the implementation spec skeleton in the house format: Defect/Goal; Fix plan; Backward compatibility; Constants vs measured reality (every timeout, limit or threshold cites the measurement it comes from and its margin); a TDD record naming each prescribed RED test per behaviour, including a literal 'Headline test: <path>' line for the headline scenario; and a task checklist with device verification ordered cheapest-first.
outcome: POLICY 9b blocks a spec that lacks the Headline test line or whose named file does not exist.

instruction: Name the check that executes each obligation you write; a spec checkbox is not a gate. The cited measurement lands in the repo as a committed artifact, the inline citation names its path, and a pin test reads both files and asserts the citation resolves.
outcome: Judge finding A3: POLICY 9a only checked that a '// measured:' substring existed, not that the evidence did.
enforcement: pin test pattern (e.g. a test that reads the measurement doc); POLICY 9a is substring-only

instruction: When you replace a citation that was shown false, never reproduce the weakness that made it false.
outcome: Stops the same false citation coming back in a new form.

instruction: When the check that executes a contract is NARROWER than the requirement sentence it certifies, write the gap into the contract ('this observable does not cover X'), then widen the check or route the gap as an owned residual. A green narrow check must never read as proof of the broad sentence.
outcome: REQ-099 F2: a one-off call on any other receiver in the same file passed all six pins.

instruction: A contract item the implementer cannot execute is a defect in the CONTRACT. Fix it there; do not work around it downstream.
outcome: Keeps the spec as the single source of truth.

instruction: Every external protocol or vendor parameter you name carries a citation for what it RETURNS. Prove an identity key is unique per UNIT, not per MODEL, and say how you know.
outcome: REQ-233 P0, judge B-2: hardware identity bytes could be ASCII aliases ('1','2','3') rather than unique ids.

instruction: For every detection form (scanner or pattern) you introduce, name in the contract the class of sites it flags that are NOT the defect, with that day's corpus count. The test harness carries one flagged and one not-flagged case.
outcome: REQ-100 verifier finding. Detection checks get explicit false-positive accounting.

instruction: A contract or plan cites a SYMBOL plus a grep-able anchor, never a bare line number, because line numbers move under the implementer's edits. Paste each named constant from the file at design time, with the command.
outcome: REQ-070/REQ-081, lesson L-20 (second sighting): a contract's constant duration was false, and a line range pointed at the very signal the clause disowned after the Developer moved the file.

instruction: When the check that executes a contract is a SOURCE PATTERN, list every spelling the construct allows (whitespace around operators, placeholder versus interpolated literal, raw query versus API argument). Declare each COVERED or EXCLUDED by name, with one mutation per covered form. One corpus example is not a population.
outcome: REQ-099 F1: check T1.4 stayed green for a delete-by-number spelled without spaces.

instruction: When a contract tells the implementer to display 'the figure X', the expression it names must be the one the code actually uses on that path. Grep it and read its definition before writing it down.
outcome: REQ-062 N-1: with a 15% tip the checkout button read $259.90 while the refusal dialog said 'would charge $226.00', a figure shown nowhere on screen. The Developer implemented the contract faithfully; the contract was wrong.

instruction: Before hand-off, diff every name a contract lists against the plan's rules for those names (an executed grep, pasted into the design) and fix any disagreement at the source. An AC that reads GREEN 'on a healthy system' must first be measured on one, with the numbers cited.
outcome: REQ-012 certification REJECTED (L-18): the contract counted items whole while the plan said per flagged order, 670 vs 27,069 on real data. The status chip could never be GREEN, and the whole arm shipped on a premise nobody had measured.

instruction: Query the code graph (query/path/explain, callers <symbol>) before enumerating call sites, scoping a blast radius, sizing a step or accepting a 'change is confined' claim. State its two limits: the graph LOCATES, but only file:line from Read/Grep may be cited, and its start-node matching is fuzzy.
outcome: Planning and verification are both enumeration problems. The graph is a navigation aid, not an oracle (L-1).

instruction: Check code-graph freshness before trusting it. A STALE graph is a finding you report (then fall back to grep), never a thing you quote. Absence from the graph never proves absence from the code.
outcome: The graph was found 35 days and 1,737 commits behind while every charter told agents to trust it (orchestrator.md:45-47). 158 of 202 lib files had changed, it named 3 deleted files and missed 25 that existed (graph_freshness.sh:4-8).

instruction: Start every decision from evidence on disk (branch git status/log, the context file, the ledger, the journal, the process table), never from memory or the last report. A report is a claim; the tree is the fact.
outcome: Operating method 1. Unmeasured.

instruction: Put the rulings a stage needs into the plan as 'questions' BEFORE it runs (an AC naming a mechanism or proof shape, a missing acceptance list, a dependency not on main, a device leg the rig cannot produce). Stop at the questions with your recommendation instead of spending developer steps guessing.
outcome: Duty 2 (consult the PO on expectations). Unmeasured.

instruction: Give the judge one explicit objective to judge every agent and artifact against: the best and most user-friendly product of its kind, matching the approved design exactly at the front and real, honest and resilient behind it.
outcome: Owner instruction 2026-10-06, to keep the swarm directed, low on tokens and unhallucinated.
owner_words: ensure the team remains directed and wasting less tokens, dont get hallucinated

instruction: Judge outcome-first, strictly: score the run's ONE owner outcome sentence end to end. Any dispatch, task, lane or change not on that outcome's path is a REVISE finding, moved to the ranked backlog. Polish certified while the outcome is unproven is waste. PASS only when the outcome path works end to end and is safe.
outcome: Directive #65 ('outcome driven development only- strict rule'). Unmeasured in the charter.

instruction: Before fixing a defect, list the whole CLASS of affected sites (callers, writers, blast radius) with a code-graph query instead of hunting the single instance.
outcome: 'Every writer of orders': graph ~297 tokens vs ~78,000 for grep-then-read of 12 files/26,027 lines (262x). Graph gave 4 real callers vs 11 mixed grep hits. One shape query found 241 candidates across 52 files.

instruction: Any fix doc or design that claims a complete list ('every writer', 'all call sites', 'each caller') must cite the query or grep that produced it. Hidden enumeration is refused.
outcome: The C10 class (a sibling site nobody listed) cost the repo more than any other. Before landing, POLICY 17 was run against 132 existing fix docs; 7 would trip.

instruction: If the evidence naming the offenders does not exist yet, instrument the system to produce it (e.g. make the error reporter print the culprit file:line) before you hunt.
outcome: crash_reporter had been discarding the widget name, which turned a 1-line fix into a 241-candidate hunt. Once it printed file:line, the hunt became a 17-line fix list.

instruction: Treat a code graph as a locator, never as proof. Only file:line from an actual Read or grep is citable, and say which parts of a claim came from the graph.
outcome: L-1. The graph's matching is fuzzy and many of its edges are unresolved (next two items).

instruction: Check every graph start-node match before using it; fuzzy matching returns unrelated nodes.
outcome: A real deleteOrder query also returned a layout helper and a markdown node.

instruction: Never read an empty graph answer as 'nothing calls this'. Fall back to grep and classify the hits.
outcome: 28,865 of 36,521 sidecar edges had unresolved targets, so empty inbound sets were common and meaningless.
enforcement: scripts/verify/graph_query.py runs the grep itself on an empty answer

instruction: If no run can satisfy an acceptance criterion, name it as a requirements defect. State both the written and the corrected observable, grade on the corrected one and report it. Never silently waive it or invent a mechanism to satisfy it.
outcome: Fifteen unsatisfiable ACs surfaced in one rig window (e.g. a build with autologin cannot render a login screen). Rule L-7.
enforcement: PO step amends the card (req-ladder rulings)

instruction: Check a code index's freshness before consulting it.
outcome: The code graph every charter consulted was 35 days / 1,737 commits stale and blind to 634 existing files.

instruction: Do not start a delivery ladder on a requirement without an enumerated Acceptance list. Fix the card first.
outcome: From the PO charter of 2026-09-05.

instruction: When amending a defective acceptance criterion, date the amendment on the card and paste the amended text verbatim into the re-dispatch prompt, so no agent depends on file timing.
outcome: No measurement given.

instruction: Put residual work the current card must not absorb into a one-line stub card for later numbering; never widen the current card.
outcome: Keeps scope bounded and nothing unowned.

instruction: Write a fix doc (spec -> plan -> tasks -> TDD record) with a '## Coverage matrix' mapping each applicable failure class to a test id. Stamp every battery/gate/analyzer result with the tree sha it ran on.
outcome: Lets reviewers cite results instead of re-running them.

instruction: State backward compatibility in every delivery: an older client version still running on a peer device.
outcome: Backward compatibility is a hard constraint for a mixed fleet.

instruction: At intake, create a product folder and have the product owner produce a market-researched backlog. Show the user the vision and backlog summary before any build starts.
outcome: No measurement given.

instruction: Analyst BLOCKED questions go to the product owner for one round, then to the user.
outcome: No measurement given.

instruction: The architect produces both the design and the implementation spec (fix doc).
outcome: No measurement given.

instruction: Produce citations; never inherit them. Every file:line, count or list comes from a command run this pass and is cited as 'Symbol (file:NN, re-read <date>)'. For safety-bearing counts paste the command and output, subtracting definition and comment hits. If you cannot run it, write 'line not re-grounded'.
outcome: 2026-08-27 REQ-030: 3 of 3 PO citations were stale, and the architect's leak argument named only 3 of 7 callers.

instruction: Make intake triage-only until the MUST wave clears. Record new findings, grounded and owned, in a findings file; promote one to a numbered requirement only if it is a MUST by severity, blocks in-flight work, or the owner asks.
outcome: The board grew 28 -> 53 while three releases shipped: finding outpaced fixing and the completion date kept moving.

instruction: Run every feature or fix outcome-first: start from ONE user-visible outcome sentence and the current path to it, and spend agents only on that path in four phases: Audit (trace the path), Fix (only its blockers), Prove (one end-to-end test), Judge (one judge on the outcome). Everything else goes into a ranked backlog for later.
outcome: Earned by REQ-323: only 56 of 319 tasks were done after more than 300M tokens read. The judged swarm had certified polish while the outcome path was never proven end to end.
owner_words: this feature has consumed exponential amount of tokens without any benefit , i need outcome results

instruction: Refuse to start an outcome run unless the caller supplies the requirement id, the outcome sentence, the current path to the outcome, and the name of the end-to-end proof test.
outcome: The run returns {stopped:'args'} before any agent is spent.

instruction: State the outcome sentence as the ONLY scope in every agent prompt, together with today's path. Work off that path is out of scope.
outcome: Keeps fixes on the outcome path rather than polish.
owner_words: outcome driven development only- strict rule

instruction: Audit read-only before fixing anything. Trace the outcome path step by step on the CURRENT tree, from the first user action to the outcome. For each step give where (file:line), whether it works, and the evidence (a covering test by name, or the code read).
outcome: Produces pathSteps with works/evidence. The run logs 'X/Y path steps work'.

instruction: In the audit, list every gap that would stop a real user. Give each an id, where it is, what it blocks, the smallest fix and the files that fix touches.
outcome: The gaps become the only Fix-phase work list.

instruction: In the audit, list the steps only the owner can do (credentials, console settings, billing, physical devices), taken from the spec, the ctx file and the decisions log. Also list the existing tests that cover parts of the path.
outcome: Owner-only steps are surfaced up front and batched, never discovered late.

instruction: The 'left' list holds ONLY product gaps on the outcome path. Process remainders (collect a log or battery, mutation-row or citation fixes, the full suite, gates, commits, doc corrections) go in 'deferred'. Deferred items run once in the merge-batch train and never block the judge.
outcome: Stops process bookkeeping from holding the outcome hostage (owner, 2026-10-08).
owner_words: outcome driven only

instruction: Work the non-outcome backlog only after the outcome is proven on the real system. Refuse the backlog workflow unless the caller names the proof (a decision id or evidence path).
outcome: Implements #65: the backlog no longer runs ahead of an unproven outcome, which is how REQ-323 burned its tokens.
owner_words: stick to outcome driven development

instruction: Refuse a swarm run without a requirement id and a brief.
outcome: Stops before any agent is spent.

instruction: Run the first spec and design rounds through three parallel lens judges (correctness, owner, testability), merged into one revision. The gate passes only when every lens PASSes.
outcome: On REQ-306, six serial rounds found issues one at a time (13 rounds, 190 min). One merged revision answers them together.

instruction: Define the three lenses. Correctness: open every load-bearing claim at its cited line and test the behaviour against the code and the safety rules. Owner: hold it to the owner's words, the rulings, the approved design and every evaluation row. Testability: every AC names an observable a run can falsify, every state, edge and failure path is covered, and nothing is unmeetable.
outcome: Complementary coverage of the spec and design.

instruction: Before any work, the judge writes its own criteria into the evaluation file (kept if already present): at most 25 measurable criteria for the objective as it applies to this requirement, each naming its check and pass bar, ordered by impact.
outcome: Implements #58: the judge scores against a per-feature evaluation file.

instruction: The PO writes the spec in spec-kit form (user stories, acceptance criteria, edge cases) as the binding oracle, at most 400 lines, with no implementation design. Every visual AC names its reference shot and exact values, and the product must match the approved design exactly.
outcome: A binding oracle that every later stage is judged against.

instruction: Include a background-truth table in every spec: each thing the user sees, and the real system event that drives it. Nothing on screen may run ahead of the real event. Acceptance greps the code against this table.
outcome: Keeps screens honest.

instruction: Cover every state the real flow needs, in the design's language. Keep approved copy verbatim unless it would be untrue for the user, and list every deviation with its reason.
outcome: Spec fidelity to the approved design.

instruction: Order the backlog by what the user feels first, not by card number. A card that moves none of the stated objective lines is not dispatched.
outcome: D6 re-ranked the backlog against six objective lines.

instruction: Prove the product as ONE end-to-end user journey before more defect cards. Build the journey by composing existing tests. Add a control that fails a vacuous pass and a mutant that stubs one step and must FAIL. Use bounded polls, never settle-all.
outcome: No end-to-end journey existed. Composition is 'the cheapest shape of work that pays', and 'the gaps it finds ARE the backlog'.

instruction: Do not re-open delivered originals whose live remainders already merged. A symptom that still shows enters as a NEW card that cites the evidence. A board-row merge record, not a tag shape, proves a merge.
outcome: 7 of 9 'parked' cards turned out to be already merged under carrier cards.

instruction: A ruling's shorthand never overrides compilable code. State the implementer form exactly (e.g. a method, not a getter), and let the context-file ruling bind the developer.
outcome: A literal reading of 'readConfirmed => read' would not compile in Dart.

instruction: Run outcome-first: stop the broad swarm and reshape around ONE owner-visible outcome. (1) One audit traces the path on the current tree and lists blocking gaps with file:line, split into code gaps and owner-only steps. (2) Developer steps fix only the code gaps on that path, RED first. (3) One end-to-end host test proves the whole path with the repo's fakes plus isolation checks. (4) One judge reviews diff and proof for traceability, security, isolation and performance. (5) Delivery through the gated delivery script. All other tasks become a ranked backlog. No safety rule is relaxed.
outcome: Measured before: 56 of 319 tasks done after more than a day and over 300M tokens, spent certifying polish while the outcome path had never been proven end to end. The first outcome judge (D168) then PASSED install-to-first-order on the fakes.
owner_words: this feature has consumed exponential amount of tokens without any benefit , i need outcome results as best restaurant pos system with self guided system in minutes for any restaurant in world

instruction: Apply outcome-first to every concurrent requirement, each with its own outcome sentence, a hard cap of 20 agents per run, and the merge gate on the final tree. Everything else in their task lists becomes a ranked backlog.
outcome: Same evidence as D163: the full ladder spent most of its agents certifying polish.
owner_words: ensure 306 and 322 also follow above mentioned principles

instruction: Outcome-driven only, strictly. Merge criteria are exactly: the outcome proven end to end (outcome tests green, outcome-path files green, outcome-pinning mutation rows killed) plus the full merge gate. Everything off the path is backlog and never blocks the merge. No new non-outcome work starts, and running work finishes only if stopping it would waste more or leave a file broken.
outcome: Narrowed REQ-306's merge criteria and moved sizing citations, a full-table battery and notices to backlog. REQ-306 later merged on this basis (D333-D337).
owner_words: outcome driven development only- strict rule
enforcement: owner directive #65; .claude/workflows/outcome-first.js; task-by-task.js refuses without args.outcomeProven (CLAUDE.md)

instruction: A backlog is not a pause. Deliver every remaining task by successive outcome-first passes run back to back, each with its own outcome sentence, path and end-to-end proof test, until every task is complete. Batch owner-only legs for the owner, and never let them idle the work.
outcome: Residual work was queued as the NEXT outcome-first pass (e.g. the newer-wins card), never parked.
owner_words: I asked to use outcome driven approach until all my tasks are complete

instruction: Scope a simulation wave to the outcome core: build only the cells where a fault touches changed code, and declare every other cell N/A with a file:line reason. Defer re-proving code the change did not touch.
outcome: Owner chose 'Outcome core' over the full matrix out of concern for token spend. Four re-proof tasks were deferred to the structural programme.
owner_words: Outcome core (Recommended)
enforcement: matrix completeness pin (every cell RUN or N/A with reason)

instruction: When cost outruns coverage, stop the wave once the outcome is proven. Merge only work that is green on its last proof, and defer the rest to a named card listing every item. Record surviving mutants as deferred per row, never delete them.
outcome: Wave 3 had spent about 3.4M tokens. The owner chose 'Stop wave 3 here', and the 7 unexplained survivors were recorded per row in REQ-326.
owner_words: Stop wave 3 here

instruction: Repairing problems that were already wrong on main (e.g. stale citations) is a separate outcome, never mixed into the current merge.
outcome: Four items were filed as next outcomes instead of widening the merge.

instruction: A citation that does not exist is a false claim. The producer fixes every rotten citation until the citation audit exits 0, before the judge runs.
outcome: Six mechanically wrong design citations were found (a non-existent file, and a line past EOF).

instruction: A process or tooling change is its own next outcome, never mixed into an in-flight feature pass.
outcome: The CI change landed as its own scripts-only branch while the feature proceeded on the old flow.

instruction: Close work that sits off the outcome path (e.g. polish on a screen no user can reach) instead of grading it. Keep its tests green and send retirement to the backlog as its own item. Adding a new door to reach it is a new feature outcome.
outcome: An unreachable screen cost 18 rounds and about 12M tokens before it was closed.
enforcement: grep for callers in lib/ as the overturn check

instruction: When an outcome sentence contradicts recorded rulings, code and tests, the sentence is the defect. Correct it at the observable and do not change the product.
outcome: A pass-8 sentence demanded a Live scene on a second-device join, contradicting four rulings. The sentence was corrected.

instruction: Fix a small defect that sits on the current outcome's own path inside that outcome, RED first. Carding it separately would mean a second branch overlapping unmerged work (duplicate risk) and a wasted full ladder.
outcome: About 8 lines in the same function were fixed in REQ-306 rather than on a separate card.

instruction: Dispatch one invariant as ONE card on the full ladder for its risk tier (e.g. 'reads scale with changes, never with age'), RED first against a committed oracle, rather than spreading it across features.
outcome: The sync-cost levers were dispatched as one invariant card.

instruction: Check every unmerged branch, not just the current one, for duplicate code: shared paths and same newly-declared names are computed by script; an agent judges whether overlap is real duplication.
outcome: The 'no duplicated code' rule had only ever looked at the branch it ran on while other unmerged branches held the same helpers.
enforcement: scripts/pipeline/branch_overlap.py; judge.md check 4 at design gate

instruction: Answer 'what calls X / who writes Y' with a graph query process so only the answer enters context; open only the named file:line with a bounded read; cite only file:line from an actual read.
outcome: Opening a 9,282-line file with 200 turns left costs ~22.2M tokens vs ~26.6k for the query; the deleteOrder question cost ~79k tokens of file reads vs a few hundred.

instruction: Measure code-graph freshness before reasoning from it; stamp the refresh basis with what the extraction actually read so the freshness check can reach green.
outcome: The graph was 35 days and 1,737 commits old, missing 25 files; later a manual refresh never stamped, so freshness read STALE forever while drift grew to 184 commits under hooks logging rc=0.

instruction: Resolve every file:line citation in design docs and flag mechanical rot (past EOF, blank line, bare delimiter); report, don't decide which line a claim belongs on.
outcome: Seven citations in one paragraph had drifted; one named lines that never held the claimed string.

instruction: Repair drifted citations by an old→new diff line map from the citation epoch; refuse deleted lines (the claim moved, a human decides); do not use anchor-text search.
outcome: The anchor heuristic repaired 11 citations with 2 wrong (landed on the declaration, not the return line); the diff map gave the correct line.

instruction: Commit external contract documents with a provenance block (url, fetched time, revision) that the parser refuses to load without.
outcome: Offline contract grading needs traceable inputs.

instruction: Run a name-agreement loop before code: every name a binding contract enumerates must appear in design and plan; grep with -F for literal names.
outcome: Names with brackets or ranges are regex metacharacters and silently mis-matched (L-18).

instruction: Emit fix docs from a template carrying every line-anchored label the doors grep for, with every class verdict left UNANSWERED for the author.
outcome: Two waves of correct fix docs were refused on labelling alone (~8 minutes per wave, twice).

instruction: Produce citations this pass (re-run grep -n); never inherit them from a spec, a report or memory; a stamped date you did not earn is a false verification claim.
outcome: Inherited citations drifted (see design_citation_audit).

instruction: Enumerate a guard ledger (reset, teardown, logout, wipe) from a grep, never sample it from the file you happened to open.
outcome: Architect BINDING.

instruction: An executing check narrower than the contract it proves must be declared as a narrowing with its own falsifier.
outcome: Architect BINDING.

instruction: A contract item the implementer cannot execute is a defect in the contract, fixed there, not worked around downstream.
outcome: Architect BINDING.

instruction: An acceptance criterion no run can satisfy is a requirements defect, fixed at the AC; grade on the corrected observable and state both forms.
outcome: PO BINDING (L-7).

instruction: Write each spec as numbered outcomes with an owner-visible outcome sentence, binding rules, scope and out-of-scope, a 'nearest existing code' table, and acceptance criteria as rows of observable, threshold, verification and source; a criterion without evidence is NOT MET.
outcome: Makes every criterion checkable and every reuse explicit (#54).
owner_words: Define measurable expectations first. A criterion without evidence is NOT MET.

instruction: Raise open rulings in the spec before the stage runs, each becoming a DAG node or a decide ruling before its outcome starts.
outcome: Rulings surfaced before, not after, a stage.
enforcement: spec judge; tasks DAG decide nodes

instruction: Fix docs carry a line-anchored 'Headline test:' line, a ticked checklist (spec, plan, result, proof, tests, mutation rows, gates, simulated verification, device leg), residuals for the coordinator, a coverage matrix by canonical class id, and a 'Lessons:' line.
outcome: The commit doors grep these anchors (L-3, agreement #9, POLICY 15).
